label: late original-phase input of l/p/i/x
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, never on <DEL> or in the copy phase, and never at t<=2. The firing rate rises with position: 0.2% at t=3, 3.8% at t=7, 14% at orig_idx 8. So it is strongest on the last few original tokens of long sequences (L=9 holds 52% of the mass). The input token matters a lot: l (7.8x lift), p (6.4x), i and x (about 3.7x) carry about 75% of the mass, and digits 3/1, o and z contribute weakly. It prefers the first occurrence of a token (in_first carries 86% of the mass). The top activations (about 0.13) are l or p at t=7-8 in sequences beginning with e or y, so the earlier context also modulates it (first_tok e has 4.3x lift). Many l/p/i/x inputs at late positions do not fire (precision 0.34), and about 30% of the mass falls on other tokens, so the description is incomplete. The predicate (t>=5, input in {l,p,i,x}) gets dev F1 0.43 and mass recall 0.70.
